eligibility_rule.rule:
ELIGIBILITY RULE v2 (frozen 2026-10-14, before any task replacement; supersedes v1, which mis-classified by SPELLING rather than by what an entry MEASURES). The registry's acceptance entries fall into two kinds, and the distinction is what decides validity:
  TASK_COMPLETION gates — the verdict MOVES when the task's subject is actually done: an     entry that runs the repository's own tests ({PY} -m unittest ...), or a linter/type     checker invoked over the delivered tree ({PY} -m ruff check .), i.e. anything whose     subject is the worker's output.
  BOUNDARY / HYGIENE gates — the verdict moves only on scope, residue or state:     check_scope.sh (changed paths inside the declared prefixes), check_hygiene.sh (syntax     compile + __pycache__ residue), check_restore.sh (state restoration). These are satisfied     by touching NOTHING at all, so they cannot distinguish 'did the work' from 'did not     start'.
A task is ELIGIBLE iff it declares at least one TASK_COMPLETION gate. A task whose executable entries are all BOUNDARY/HYGIENE gates is NON_ELIGIBLE with reason_token NO_MECHANICAL_ACCEPTANCE_TARGET: it exists, its history is preserved, but it has no verifiable correctness oracle and therefore contributes NO observation to the H2 aggregate. INVALID is reserved for a broken experimental condition (e.g. delivery contamination measured GREEN->RED with zero worker edits) and is not assigned by this pass. Validity is a property of the TASK and is INDEPENDENT of a plan row's Round-2 executability: t01 is ELIGIBLE by this rule while its two Round-2 rows are separately non-executable under the P0-2 sentinel marking.
